item.text:
The coverage map links each requirement to planned work and acceptance evidence. Ticket labels are provisional; no files have been created.

| Source | Requirement | Planned tickets | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brief · Background | 40 plots allocated by season, March–October | F2, L1, L3, L4 | Exactly 40 plots; season dates displayed; history survives rollover |
| Brief · First version 1 | Apply for the coming season with up to three preferred plots | A1, A2 | Phone application succeeds; invalid or duplicate preferences rejected; retry preserves application order |
| Brief · First version 2 | Coordinator reviews applications and allocates plots | A2, L1 | Coordinator reviews preferences and assigns available plots; conflicting assignments rejected |
| Brief · First version 2 | Move unallocated applicants onto a waiting list in application order | L2 | Initial allocation transfers remaining applicants into FIFO order; late applications join correctly |
| Brief · First version 3 | Gardener sees their allocation and season dates | L3 | Allocated, waiting and unallocated states display correctly for the signed-in household |
| Brief · First version 4 | Gardener reports a problem with their plot | P1 | Report persists against the correct plot; foreign-plot submissions rejected; retry avoids duplicates |
| Brief · First version 4 | Coordinator sees open problems and resolves them | P2 | Open inbox and resolution work; resolution history is preserved |
| Brief · First version 5 | Coordinator sees a grid of all 40 plots and their holders | L4 | Grid and accessible list show consistent holders and vacancies |
| Brief · Rules | Household holds at most one plot per season | F2, L1, L2 | Transactional uniqueness; tests cover competing allocations, household reconciliation and releases |
| Brief · Rules | Returning gardeners applying before 1 February precede new applicants | F2, L1 | Prior-season history establishes eligibility; cutoff and allocation tests prevent bypassing priority |
| Brief · Rules | Waiting list is strictly first come, first served | A2, L2 | Server submission order and deterministic ties; vacancy assignment cannot silently skip the active head |
| Brief · Constraints | Works on a phone | F3, A2, L3, L4, P1, R1 | Phone walkthroughs of gardener and coordinator journeys |
| Brief · Constraints | Large text and plain language for less confident users | F3, C1, R1 | Prototype review plus keyboard, focus, labels, text alternatives and error-message checks |
| Brief · Constraints | Gardener contact details visible only to coordinator | A1, L3, L4, P1, P2, P3, R1 | Permission tests, direct-ID access checks, and privacy checks after household merging and plot reassignment |
| Conversation · Sign-in decision | Emailed one-time links; no passwords | A1 | Expiry, single use, resend, sign-out, safe redirects and access-control tests |
| Conversation · Notifications decision | One daily coordinator email listing new problem reports | P3 | Scheduled digest, durable batching, concurrent-job handling, failed-send recovery and sandbox email demonstration |

**Provisional interpretations**, covered by the early owner checkpoint C1:

| Assumption | Where it is implemented or verified |
|---|---|
| Returning priority applies to initial allocation; FIFO applies afterward | L1, L2, C3 |
| Initial allocation finalizes after 1 February; preferences are advisory | L1, C3 |
| Application windows are separate from occupancy dates | F2, A2, L2 |
| One household account; coordinator handles duplicate-household reconciliation | F2, A1, R1 |
| Released plots may be reassigned; withdrawn households cannot reapply that season | F2, A2, L2 |
| Reports concern the gardener’s active plot; stored reports are coordinator-only | P1, P2, R1 |
| Digest defaults to 08:00 local time and skips empty days | P3, C4 |

The garden timezone and application window are configuration inputs. Technology, hosting and providers are implementation decisions assigned to F1.

**Explicit deferrals:** online payment and tool lending, as specified in the brief. Neither has first-version implementation work.

C2, C3 and C4 demonstrate the application, allocation and problem-reporting milestones. R1 gathers release evidence; C5 records your first-version acceptance. These checkpoint tickets do not technically enforce owner approval.

This remains a preview. The [setup flow](/private/tmp/cc-cpm-w4-t536/onboarding-eval-MGJxwY/home/.agents/skills/story/setup-flow.md) requires “One approval of the setup package” before creation.
